chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Hasan ibn Fazzal, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Imran al-Halbi, who said: 'I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)'

about a man who performed Tawaf around the House (Kaaba) for three circuits of the obligatory (Tawaf). Then he found empty space from the House, so he entered it. How should he deal with it? He (peace be upon him) said: 'He should complete his Tawaf, and he has opposed the Sunnah, therefore he must repeat his Tawaf.'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on Tawaf if one enters the Kaaba during the circumambulation?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Kafi highlights the juristic distinction between the validity (sihha) and perfection (kamal) of Tawaf; while the three circuits suffice for the obligatory duty, entering the Kaaba disrupts the continuity required by the Sunnah. Scholars note this reflects the Shia emphasis on adhering to the Prophet's specific ritual mannerisms, where a deviation, though not invalidating the core act, necessitates repetition to achieve the ideal form of worship.

en.hubeali:
A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Al Hassan Bin Fazzal, from Hammad Bin Isa, from Imran Al Halby who said, 
‘I asked Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>

about a man who performed Tawaaf by the House (Kaaba), three circuits from the Obligatory one. Then he found empty space from the House (Kaaba). So he entered it. How should he deal with it?’ So heasws said: ‘He should fulfil his Tawaaf, and he has opposed the Sunnah, therefore upon him is his Tawaaf (to repeat)’.
en.sarwar: 3. A number of our people have narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from al-Hassan ibn al-Faddal from Hammad ibn ‘Isa from ‘Imran al-Halabiy who has said the following: “I once asked abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam,

about a man who performs three Tawaf (walking around the House) of obligatory nature; then he finds an opportunity to enter the House and he enters the House and about what he is required to do. He (the Imam) said, ‘He must perform Qada’ (compensatory) of his Tawaf, because he has done against the Sunnah; he must perform Tawaf again.’”
